source_packet.title: Why calling for a ‘kill switch’ is the wrong way to think about reining in AI
source_packet.evidence:
explain: The idea of a single emergency switch makes AI governance look like a matter of one decisive act. Wintermeier argues that this image hides the distributed infrastructure of advanced systems and the human decisions that shape their behavior before any emergency occurs.
limitation: This is a rhetoric- and governance-centered expert commentary, not an empirical evaluation of frontier AI controls. It describes particular incidents and policy proposals from 2026; those circumstances are context for the author's argument, not a systematic sample of AI failures.
thesis: The idea of a single emergency switch makes AI governance look like a matter of one decisive act. Wintermeier argues that this image hides the distributed infrastructure of advanced systems and the human decisions that shape their behavior before any emergency occurs.
reasoning: The essay treats a kill switch as a political and technological metaphor rather than only a device specification. A switch implies a bounded machine, an identifiable point of control and an operator who can intervene once a problem is visible. That mental picture is a poor fit for advanced AI deployed across interconnected services, data centers, models and users. Even if a particular model can be disabled, the metaphor does not specify who could halt associated processes or what would remain active elsewhere. Wintermeier connects this limitati
qualification: This is a rhetoric- and governance-centered expert commentary, not an empirical evaluation of frontier AI controls. It describes particular incidents and policy proposals from 2026; those circumstances are context for the author's argument, not a systematic sample of AI failures.

source_packet.title: Prompt‐based emotional scaffolding in generative AI : Effects on self‐regulated learning and socio‐emotional outcomes
source_packet.evidence:
findings: All three groups improved on immediate conceptual-knowledge and learning-transfer tests; however, condition-by-time comparisons were not statistically significant for either outcome (p = .980 and p = .953). At the four-week follow-up, knowledge and transfer change likewise did not differ significantly between groups. Both SRL-based chatbot groups showed larger improvements in enjoyment and reductions in boredom than the general-purpose ChatGPT group. Emotional SRLbot also showed higher task-level performance and reflection indicators in the interaction traces. Hopelessness fell across all groups without a differential treatment effect, and self-efficacy and chatbot trust did not show clear b
methods: A preregistered randomized classroom experiment assigned 144 Danish high-school students to standard ChatGPT, an AI chatbot that guided self-regulated learning (SRLbot), or the same approach with emotional support (Emotional SRLbot), with 48 participants in each condition. One learning session lasted about 25 minutes. Tests and surveys were administered before and after, and 85 students completed a four-week follow-up. Interaction traces were cod
interpretation: The authors interpret the findings as preliminary support for combining AI prompts about planning, monitoring and reflection with encouragement sensitive to students' emotional states. An intervention that makes learning feel better and increases momentary self-regulatory behavior is not yet evidence of lasting independent learning gains. Theoretical expectations about emotional regulation pathways were not themselves fully tested as causal media
limitations: The intervention lasted only one 25-minute session. The pretest and follow-up knowledge measures had internal consistency below .60, making the learning estimates less reliable. Only 85 of the original 144 returned for follow-up, and dropout related to prior AI experience and initial boredom. Some self-report and trace-based measures diverged, and trace coding was aggregated across each session rather than modeling the sequence of regulatory behaviors. Several outcome comparisons were tested and longer-term effects remain uncertain.
finding: Tailored agents increased enjoyment and reduced boredom relative to ChatGPT; emotional scaffolding also strengthened observed task-level regulation. Immediate learning gains occurred in all groups, without a statistically significant advantage for the tailored agents.
approach: Preregistered three-arm classroom experiment (144 students; 48 per condition) comparing ChatGPT, an SRL-supporting chatbot and an emotionally supportive SRL chatbot; 85 completed a four-week follow-up.
explain: In a randomized high-school trial, adding self-regulation prompts and emotional support changed how students felt and engaged during the task, but did not establish superior knowledge or transfer gains.
limitation: A single 25-minute intervention, attrition at follow-up, and weak reliability in some knowledge tests limit the learning and retention claims.

source_packet.title: A new task of sustained attention: investigating the role of ADHD symptoms and response time variability in a task requiring children and adolescents to wait
source_packet.evidence:

After visually inspecting the data, one adolescent who made 17 omission errors on the SART was removed since the number largely deviated from other participants and was considered an outlier. This resulted in a sample of 25 out of 28 children (M 10.6 years, SD 1.0), and 47 out of 49 adolescents (M 17.6 years, SD 0.8). The means and standard deviations of each outcome variable were summariz

Forty-nine adolescents aged between 15 and 18 years (M 17.57 years, SD 0.76; 33 females) were recruited from local secondary schools (n 6) and from an undergraduate course in psychology at the university (n 43). Participation in this study required no known neurological condition, pervasive developmental disorder, or hi
interpretation: Here we introduce a new sustained attention task, the Disappearance Detection Task (DDT), designed to be more monotonous and demanding on the sustained attention system than the SART. The DDT was designed to make individuals sustain their attention and engage in motor preparation without engaging any other task-related processes such as sensory perception, decision-making, or motor execution, which occurs during the SART. explain: This study aimed to investigate the relationship between response time variability and levels of ADHD symptoms both in this new, low-arousal sustained attention task and in the Sustained Attention to Response Task (SART).

source_packet.title: The psychology of learning with generative AI in foreign language education: building a theory of metacognition, trust, and human–AI co-regulation through a systematic review
source_packet.evidence:
findings: The 51 included studies yielded four overlapping domains: metacognition/self-regulated learning (Lai et al., 2026) , trust (El Hosayny et al., 2026) , human-AI co-regulation/collaboration (Zakaria et al., 2025) , and AI literacy/learner agency (El Hosayny et al., 2026) . Because studies could address multiple constructs, these counts are overlapping contributions and should not be summed. The following sections synthesize evidence within and across these domains. The five research questions are addressed by integrating the empirical evidence synthesized in Section 4 with the theoretical interpretation developed in Sections 5.1-5.3 (Table 2 ). The synthesis indicates that the educational valu
methods: This study employed a theory-building systematic review to synthesize empirical evidence on the psychological processes underlying generative-AI-supported foreign language learning. The review followed PRISMA 2020 for study identification, screening, and reporting and used qualitative thematic and conceptual synthesis to develop a theoretical account. The review focused on three interconnected mechanisms: metacognition, trust, and human-AI co-reg
interpretation: This systematic review examined the psychological processes through which learners engage with generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) in foreign language education. Drawing on 51 empirical studies, it moved beyond whether GenAI improves particular language skills to examine how learners understand, evaluate, regulate, and coordinate their interactions with generative systems. Metacognition, trust, and human-AI co-regulation emerged as interco
limitations: Several limitations qualify the interpretation of the findings. The 51 studies varied substantially in participants, research designs, learning contexts, AI applications, and operationalization's of psychological constructs, which limits direct comparison across studies. Moreover, the evidence base is relatively recent and rapidly evolving; findings associated with particular GenAI systems may therefore change as technologies and patterns of use develop. The review has methodological limitations related to its singleauthor design. Screening, full-text assessment, and thematic coding were conducted by the sole author without independent review

limitation: Several limitations qualify the interpretation of the findings.

source_packet.title: Designing generative AI–powered reflective learning dashboards for enhancing self-regulated learning in higher education
source_packet.evidence:
findings: Quantitative results revealed significant improvements in self-regulated learning behaviours, time on task, login frequency and academic performance (p < .001), indicating strong effects on both cognitive and behavioural dimensions of learning.
methods: Using a quasi-experimental design, 180 undergraduate students participated in a 12-week intervention comparing traditional instructor feedback with AI-generated reflective feedback. Quantitative results revealed significant improvements in self-regulated learning behaviours, time on task, login frequency and academic performance (p < .001), indicating strong effects on both cognitive and behavioural dimensions of learning.
explain: This study contributes a scalable, human-centred and ethically grounded model for improving both learning outcomes and learner experience in digital education environments.

source_packet.title: Faster! Louder! Brighter! How the attention economy overwhelmed children’s TV
source_packet.evidence:
explain: Media quality cannot be reduced to screen-time totals or educational subject matter. Kucirkova argues that the rhythm of children's media shapes opportunities to reflect, understand a story and connect emotionally: constantly shifting cues may capture attention while leaving too little space to process.
limitation: This is a research-informed essay drawing on children's media comparisons and the Kids' Slow Media Project, not an experiment showing that all fast-paced media harms children or that slower media always produces better learning.
thesis: Media quality cannot be reduced to screen-time totals or educational subject matter. Kucirkova argues that the rhythm of children's media shapes opportunities to reflect, understand a story and connect emotionally: constantly shifting cues may capture attention while leaving too little space to process.
reasoning: Kucirkova distinguishes the amount of time spent watching from the time a story gives a child to interpret an event. Rapid cuts, songs, and rewards may continually restart attention; a coherent narrative, repetition, and pauses can leave space for prediction, emotion, and memory. She argues that a screen can look engaging without supporting the reflective work its lesson requires.
qualification: This is a research-informed essay drawing on children's media comparisons and the Kids' Slow Media Project, not an experiment showing that all fast-paced media harms children or that slower media always produces better learning.

draft.headline: Comparing AI's Impact on Learning
draft.deck: Three studies explore the impact of AI on learning and engagement, yet each highlights significant limitations. How do these varied interventions truly affect long-term learning and sustained attention in students?
draft.letter: Three studies delve into the impact of AI on learning and engagement. The first, involving SRL-based chatbots, found that while all groups improved in knowledge and learning transfer, the differences were not statistically significant. However, the chatbots enhanced enjoyment and reduced boredom. The second study, using reflective learning dashboards, reported significant improvements in self-regulated learning behaviors, time on task, login frequency, and academic performance. Meanwhile, the third study by Jinggangshan University researchers found that AI-assisted writing showed the highest observed writing quality when open collaboration was present, but did not lead to the strongest independent performance. Despite these positive outcomes, all studies have limitations, such as brief interventions and incomplete follow-ups. How do these varied interventions truly affect long-term learning and sustained attention in students?

tension.title: Long-Term Effects of AI on Learning
tension.text: While studies show that AI can enhance enjoyment and reduce boredom, they do not definitively prove long-term improvements in learning and sustained attention. The first study's intervention was limited to a single 25-minute session, and the knowledge tests had low reliability. The second study, while effective, only lasted 12 weeks and did not fully address long-term effects. The third study's offloading framework requires independent validation, and the six-class allocation may have confounded condition with class, timetable, and cohort. How do these varied interventions truly affect long-term learning and sustained attention in students?

signals.text: Both studies explore the impact of AI on self-regulated learning. The second study, using reflective learning dashboards, reported significant improvements in self-regulated learning behaviors, time on task, login frequency, and academic performance. signals.title: Analyzing the Effects of Fast-Paced Media on Children’s Attention Compared to Slower Media
signals.text: The Guardian article by Kucirkova discusses how the rhythm of children's media, such as fast-paced TV shows, can capture attention but leave little space for reflection and emotional connection. In contrast, slower media allows for more coherent narratives and pauses, which can support prediction, emotion, and memory. However, the study does not show that all fast-paced media harms children or that slower media always produces better learning. Meanwhile, the scholarly study by Jinggangshan University researchers found that AI-assisted writing showed the highest observed writing quality when open collaboration was present, but did not lead to the strongest independent performance. The study's limitations include the six-class allocation, which may have confounded condition with class, timetable, and cohort. Additionally, Week 8 measured near transfer rather than delayed or cross-genre transfer, and the offloading framework requires independent validation.
